newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Gateway to buy Advanced Logic for $194 million.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Gateway to buy Advanced Logic for $194 million.

text.p: Computer maker Gateway 2000 Inc. said Thursday it agreed to acquire Advanced Logic Research Inc. for about $194 million in a move by the PC seller to expand in the corporate market.
PC direct marketer Gateway said it would buy Advanced Logic for $15.50 a share.

North Sioux City, S.D.-based Gateway said the acquisition is part of its push into the lucrative corporate market for servers, or computers that manage networks, and expects the deal to immediately begin boosting earnings.
"We expect it to be additive or accretive to earnings," Ted Waitt, Gateway's chairman, told reporters on a conference call.

"I can't get into specifically what kind of numbers are there, because there are a lot of synergies that will play out over time," he said, adding the combination will result in enhanced revenues and cost savings.

Gateway said it anticipates a one-time, non-cash charge for the write-off of research and development in process for Advanced Logic. This charge is expected in the third quarter, but the company said an engineering study will have to be completed before an estimate can be made.

The move into servers, or powerful central computers in networks, is part of Gateway's expansion into the business market. Gateway's large business accounts make up 36 percent of sales, which totalled $5 billion in 1996, and servers and high-end workstations are more profitable than PCs.

"This ties in very well as a natural extension of our major push into the corporate market and our desire to increase our basis there," Waitt said. "By adding a server offering to our product line, we feel there's just tremendous synergies to offer."
Advanced Logic, based in Irvine, Calif., will operate as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Gateway and continue to market products under the Advanced Logic brand name through resellers.

Advanced Logic products may eventually be branded and sold through Gateway's direct marketing approach. But the Gateway brand, currently sold on a made-to-order basis via catalog and telephone orders, the Internet and special Gateway "country stores", will never be sold through resellers, Waitt said.

"There is no chance that Gateway-branded products will be offered through the indirect channel, but there is a chance we will look to expand ALR product offerings," he said, adding however that would be done through Advanced Logic.
The companies said the deal will result in a continued expansion of their work forces.

Advanced Logic's largest stockholder, Wearnes Technology Ltd., together with Advanced Logic Chief Executive Gene Lu and two other board members, have agreed to tender their shares. They collectively hold about 42 percent of Advanced Logic outstanding shares.
Lu will remain president of Advanced Logic and will become a vice president and officer of Gateway. The tender offer is expected to be completed by the end of July.
News of the acquisition comes just days after Gateway said it would not meet second quarter revenue expectations because of a later-than-usual pick up in sales.

"I think this is a very positive move for Gateway because it will allow them to more quickly enter the server marketplace," Matt Russo, an analyst for Sands Brothers Co. said, adding the Advanced Logic brand is highly regarded.
"The purchase price seems very fair and ... it will have a positive effect on their bottom line," Russo added.
Gateway shares closed up $1.125 at $33.125 on the New York Stock Exchange, and Advanced Logic rose $2.125 to $14.125 on Nasdaq.
